reviews.text: Touristy for sure, but the cochinillo is the real thing. Book weeks ahead or you will not get in.
Cramped and loud downstairs, charming upstairs. Service was warm even though we barely spoke Spanish.
Huevos rotos are exactly as good as everyone says. Go for lunch, it is quieter.
Great for a group. We were six and they squeezed us in without fuss.
Lively but insanely crowded by 8pm. Come early if you want a seat.
Expensive for what it is, but the variety is fun with kids who cannot agree on anything.
Standing room only on a Saturday night. Loud, fun, not a place for a quiet dinner.
Quiet terrace with a view of the palace. Perfect spot to read for an hour.
Coffee is fine, the setting is the point. Very calm in the morning.
Best flat white in Malasaña. Tiny, no laptops, in and out.
Standing at the counter with a cortado is the move. Friendly baristas.
Laptop friendly and plenty of plugs. I worked here solo for three hours and nobody minded.
Quiet in the mornings, gets lively after 6pm. Good wifi.
One of the best cocktail bars anywhere. Get the Chipotle Chillón.
Tiny and packed, expect to wait. Worth it. Definitely a night out, not a quiet drink.
Cheap vermouth, great tortilla, standing room only. Classic Madrid.
Squeeze in at the bar. Budget friendly and full of locals.
Wild flavours, deafening music. Not a romantic dinner, more of an event.
Pricey for small plates but genuinely unlike anything else.
Cocido is a two hour commitment and worth every minute. Family run, very traditional.
Cash only when we went. Small dining room, quiet, no music.
Overwhelming in the best way. Give it three hours minimum.
Free entry in the last two hours but the queue is long. Kids got bored after an hour.
Guernica alone justifies the ticket. Much calmer than the Prado.
Quiet on a weekday morning. Good for a solo visit.
Rent a rowboat, it is cheap and the kids loved it. Great family afternoon.
Huge and calm once you get away from the lake. Free.
Fun if you want to dance until 6am. Very young crowd, very loud.
Drinks are overpriced and the queue was 40 minutes. Nightlife, not a bar.
Dark, quiet, proper classic cocktails. Great for a conversation.
Downstairs is intimate. Easily the most relaxed cocktail bar in Malasaña.
Croquetas only, and that is all they need. Cheap, tiny, always packed.
Standing on the street with a plate of croquetas and a beer. Budget perfection.
Order a drink, get a mountain of free tapas. Absurd value, absolutely chaotic.
Loud, cramped, cheap. Great for a group of students, terrible for a date.
Churros con chocolate at 2am after a night out is a Madrid rite of passage.
Touristy but genuinely good. Open nearly all night. Kids love it.
Casa Dani's tortilla is the reason to come. Get there before the lunch rush.
A real neighbourhood market, not a tourist one. Cheap and quiet midweek.
Sherry only, no photos, no tips. Feels unchanged since the 1930s.
Quiet, dim, no music. The bartender chalks your tab on the counter.
Serious flamenco, not a tourist revue. Expensive but unforgettable.
Book the dinner seating for the better view. A proper night out.
Weekends only, and almost nobody knows about it. The most peaceful garden in Madrid.
Very quiet, lots of shade. Bring a book. Free entry.
Beautiful old taberna, organic produce, calm at lunch.
The set lunch menu is good value. Quiet enough to actually talk.
